Shopify Storefront Proposal

Relove Vintage Apparel — Shopify Storefront Proposal

Client: Relove Vintage Apparel — vintage and vintage-inspired women's apparel
Prepared by: LitOS/LitGroup
Date: August 17, 2026
1

Proposed scope

1.1 Platform

Move the storefront to Shopify.

This proposal covers Shopify design & development only. Backend data migration (products, orders, customers) is not included — that's handled by a separate team, LitExtension (a sister brand), who provide their own estimate and quote once the volume to migrate is known.

1.2 Theme

Foundation theme: Ella — free through the Litos/HaloThemes partnership.

Ella is purpose-built for fashion and apparel stores, and covers a number of the improvements below natively rather than through custom development: grouped mega menu, search-as-icon opening a predictive search overlay, hero slider with hover-revealed controls, product sliders, Quick View as a corner icon on the product card, image-led collection banner sections, collection filtering, and product galleries in both thumbnail and stacked-image layouts.

The store is rebuilt by customizing Ella — not designed from scratch — carrying over the existing brand palette, typography and logo.

1.3 Core build

  • Theme setup & brand styling — Ella configured to the current brand identity: pink and black palette, serif display typography, logo.
  • Page templates — homepage, collection template, product template, cart and account, plus the content pages: FAQ, Contact us, Returns / Return Policy, Privacy Policy, Terms of Service, and the app download page.
  • Site container widened — content runs to a wider container across every template, so the storefront no longer sits in a narrow column.
  • Responsive storefront — verified on desktop, tablet and mobile.
  • Full storefront review & testing before launch, so everything is verified working before the store goes live.

1.4 Front-end improvements

Header & navigation

  • Header made more compact — reduced overall height with the announcement bar tightened, giving a lighter header appropriate to a fashion store.
  • Menu consolidated — items grouped into shorter parent categories instead of listed flat, and the Home item removed. The four capsule and series links currently sitting on the main row already appear inside the Collections dropdown, so they fold into it; the garment categories (Tops, Bottoms, Sets, Dresses) group under a single Shop parent.
  • Search field replaced by an icon — clicking it opens a full search overlay with predictive results, which suits a fashion storefront better than a permanently visible input.

Hero

  • Prev / next arrows revealed on hover rather than shown at all times.
  • Dots removed, so the slider reads as a clean full-bleed image.

What's New

  • Pagination control removed and the section rebuilt as a slider, so new arrivals browse horizontally instead of paging through numbered screens.
  • Quick View restyled as a small icon in the corner of the product card, in place of the full-width bar that currently covers the bottom of the image.

Collections section

A new image-led collection section added to the homepage — large lifestyle tiles that open into their collection, so the homepage leads with collections rather than only individual products.

Connect with us

The Connect with us block moved down to sit directly above the footer, or folded into the footer itself, so it no longer interrupts the shopping journey mid-page.

Footer

Rebuilt with a proper column structure, brand styling, newsletter signup, social row, payment icons and a legal bar — in place of the current off-centre link grid.

Direction reference:

Collection page

  • Pagination moved below the product grid, where it belongs in the browsing flow, instead of sitting above the products alongside the filter and sort controls.
  • Filter button restyled in the brand pink or in black, so it reads as a deliberate part of the design.

Product page

The image gallery rebuilt in one of two layouts, confirmed before build:

  • Thumbnail strip beside or beneath a large main image, with click-to-enlarge, or
  • Large stacked image list, where the full set of product photos runs down the page at full size.
